references.text: The same context where Joshua receives instructions to choose twelve men, one from each tribe, to take stones from the Jordan.
The Israelites do as Joshua commands and take twelve stones from the Jordan, one for each tribe.
The priests carry the ark of the covenant before the people, corresponding to the reference to the Lord's ark in the verse.
Twelve stones representing the twelve tribes of Israel, a recurring motif in Israelite tradition.
Moses set up twelve stone pillars for the twelve tribes of Israel, the same symbolism as here.
Reference to the twelve tribes of Israel mentioned in Joshua 4:5.
Elijah takes twelve stones according to the number of the tribes of Jacob's sons, the same symbolism with twelve stones for twelve tribes.
The new Jerusalem has twelve gates with the names of the twelve tribes of Israel, and twelve foundation stones with the names of the apostles.
